**Geoshift: Lunar South Pole Navigator**

Geoshift is a web-based tool designed to make exploring and comparing lunar landing sites easier. It focuses on the 13 NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions near the Moon's South Pole. Using live data from NASA JPL Horizons, Geoshift shows the positions of the Sun and Earth as seen from each landing site.

With Geoshift, users can check when a location receives sunlight, how long it may remain illuminated, and whether Earth is visible for direct communication. Users can also compare different landing sites, explore different dates, and watch the movement of the Sun and Earth through an interactive sky view.

Our goal is to turn complex space data into information that is easy to understand and use. This can help mission planners make better decisions when choosing landing locations and planning surface activities. It is important because astronauts need reliable sunlight for power and a stable communication link with Earth to carry out their missions safely.
details:
Geoshift: Lunar South Pole Navigator

Geoshift is a web-based platform that helps users explore and compare the 13 NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions near the Moon's South Pole. Our main idea is to make complex space data easier to understand and use.

The platform connects with NASA JPL Horizons to retrieve astronomical data about the Sun and Earth from different lunar landing locations. Using this data, Geoshift shows when sunlight reaches a landing site and when Earth is visible from that location. This information is important because astronauts need sunlight for solar power and a reliable communication link with Earth during their missions.

Users can select different landing sites, choose dates, explore changes over time, and compare conditions between locations. The platform also includes an interactive sky observatory, timeline controls, date filters, and an astronaut briefing feature that helps users understand the results.

Our goal is to help mission planners explore different landing locations more easily and make better-informed decisions. It can also help students, educators, and space enthusiasts understand the challenges of exploring the Moon.

We developed Geoshift as a web application using modern web technologies, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. We also integrated the NASA JPL Horizons API to retrieve dynamic astronomical data. A local proxy server handles API requests and helps the application communicate with the data source.

What makes Geoshift different is that it brings site comparison, sunlight analysis, Earth visibility, and time-based visualization together in one simple interface. While developing it, we considered the Moon's unusual lighting conditions, communication limitations, accuracy of astronomical data, and the importance of making the information easy for different types of users to understand.

Our aim is to make lunar mission planning more accessible and support future exploration of the Moon's South Pole.
